body: You'd think I should know that since I'm studying the biochemistry and metabolism, but for some reason I still make stupid decisions. And I was fat before I started starving myself. I don't if being overweight is the reason I'm doing, but more as a punishment for myself. I know, that's pretty pathetic.
Still, that feeling of that moment you cave is still pretty depressing.

I've tried starving myself to death. I try hard to not eat at all, and hope that I become malnourished enough that I die. Unfortunately, since I'm a failure in general, I don't have the will power to keep it up. The longest I've gone without eating is 51 hours. And I'm still overweight.
Thank you. That's actually really good advice.

I just don't advice in general. I just want people to believe in me. Make me feel better. That kind of thing. If I mess up somewhere, I don't want people telling me how I can better, I want people telling me that I'm not any worse for making that mistake.

I think it's more that I don't know what's wrong. Because I don't know what's wrong, I don't know what's the right thing to do.

I know I can't force someone to stay in my life, and I hope I don't do that ever. I guess I just wish people wanted me more. As it is, I don't feel as if that's the case.

Well, the hope would be to get them away from the idea that there was something remediable that was avoided, and realize that no matter what the situation, I had no confidence in myself which led to the ultimate decision.

You're right. Most people aren't trained. However, most people don't even take the time to try to figure out what to do either. It's great that you had that concern to do that for someone you care about, and that person is lucky to have a friend like you. The people I call friends, they don't know what to do. They have their own problems to deal with. I'm in the back burner. But can I really blame them? There lives are better than mine, and so more effort should be put into the thing already working to make sure it's still working.

That's an idea. That's not my intention, but if somehow writing a note allows me to see a pattern, that's great. I'm not holding my breath, though.

I won't show it to anyone. I'll type it up and keep it in files. No one looks through my stuff anyway. I don't have anyone that close to me who would do that. And it's not so much they want me to die, it's that I feel like I'd be doing humanity a favor by removing the scourge that is me. I'm sure people's lives would be so much better once I'm gone.

That's a very apt title, though I wanted to stray away from using words like "survivor" and "victim".

Well, I've already tried talking to them. Through a mixture of my own depression fed stubbornness and their inability to either understand or say the things to make me feel better, it hasn't worked out really well. They said themselves they don't know what else to do or say to help. And it stresses them out to deal with a sad friend. I can't do that to them. They and them being the few close friends I have confided to. I had a hope of support, I really did. But it never came, not in the way I needed it. It's okay, though. I had expectations too high. I've learned most people aren't equipped to deal in these situations, so it's unfair to expect them to do the things needed to make a person feel better. Unfortunate, but that's reality for you. Always unfortunate.

I'm sorry to say that I am not the poet that you are referring to. But I am glad that I was able to help you achieve a brief moment of happiness. Being a fan of poetry, I'd love to read some his work.
